alyssa: Heads up — after merge r5123 we see a P99 latency increase on euw2 A10 cluster for small-chat workload. Canary shows p99 ~420ms -> 950ms. CI perf test failed: see logs from canary job. Anyone on call?
rahul: Looking. Quick glance at perf artifacts — heavy KV cache evictions during the window. kvcache.evictions per-sec spiked ~6x.
mina: I also noticed batching hist changed — huge number of tiny batches (1-3) instead of 8-12. Heuristic seems to underbatch for short requests. Could be correlated with kernel selection latency.
jorge: Kernel selector logs: many falls back to generic_kernel for forward pass on model-3b due to fallback condition: "tensor_core_candidate=false" from selector. Fallbacks add ~200-300us per-token. Example log snippet: ```[2026-03-17T12:03:21Z] selector: model=model-3b hw=A10 candidate=false reason="unsupported-dtype/shape" selected=generic_kernel```
alyssa: CI output (excerpt): ```FAILED perf/canary/euw2-a10: p99_latency_ms=950 (baseline=420) regression_pct=126%``` ci-bot: perf-run-214 failed step test/perf-euw2-a10 (regression)
rahul: I uploaded a flamegraph to build artifacts: /artifacts/214/flamegraph.svg — top contributors are: kernel_dispatch (~34%), kvcache::evict_worker (~22%), net::egress_io (~12%).
mina: The net egress numbers jumped too — looks like transient NIC queueing. Possibly noisy neighbor from adjacent tenant observed on node 7. Network counters show tx_queue_full events.
jorge: Correlating node-level logs: at 12:02 we had an autoscaler rebalance that migrated some containers; that coincides with spike. Also merge r5123 changed kernel selection threshold "min_batch_for_tensor_core" from 4 -> 6. That makes selector more conservative for short seqs.
alyssa: So plausible chain: selector more conservative -> more generic kernels -> higher compute per-token; combined with kvcache churn (evictions) causing more memory IO -> NIC egress queuing -> p99 spike.
rahul: Quick repro on staging (single node) with synthetic skewed traffic reproduced tiny-batch distribution when selector threshold=6. Reverting threshold to 4 fixes batch size and p99 back to ~430ms.
mina: I attached a small config diff to the thread: ```{"kernel_selector": {"min_batch_for_tensor_core": 4}}```
jorge: Candidate action plan: 1) hold rollout for euw2-a10 (ops-bot can set hold), 2) revert r5123 partial (selector change) or patch to lower threshold, 3) investigate kvcache eviction spike root cause (profiling), 4) add metric alert for tx_queue_full and evict rate.
ops-bot: rollout-hold applied to canary euw2-a10 by @alyssa — reason: p99 regression after r5123 :warning:
ci-bot: created revert PR r5123-revert-selector-threshold (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runs/pull/5123/revert) and kicked perf CI on the revert.
alyssa: Can someone run a quick bisect? If reverting selector change fixes perf we can cut a patch and unhold. If not, we dig deeper into kvcache GC heuristics.
rahul: Starting bisect now — I'll test commits between r5118..r5125. Will post minimal repro commands.
mina: For profiling: use `local-run --profile --capture=kvcache,net,dispatch --seq-len=32 --qps=120` and attach artifacts. That reproduces the tiny-batch behavior.
jorge: Note: H100 clusters unaffected in canary — only A10 nodes show regression, so likely kernel selector + A10 tensor core availability mismatch. Good to narrow scope.
alyssa: Thanks team. @rahul please ping when bisect narrows to a commit. If revert passes perf CI, we'll unhold and apply hotfix. :thumbsup:
rahul: Update: bisect found r5121 (the selector threshold change) as the first bad commit. Revert patch reduces p99 to 440ms in staged canary. Will open revert PR now.
alyssa: Perfect — once CI green we revert in prod. Also create ticket for kvcache eviction root cause and NIC noisy neighbor mitigation runbook.
mina: adding short-term mitigations to ticket: temporarily increase kvcache capacity on euw2 a10 pool and add tx_queue_full alert to SRE dashboard.
alyssa: closing loop — thanks everyone.
